title: Google Ads vs Local Services Ads for small business marketing - Google Ads

facts.fact: The article's example business goal is to increase online sales by 20% over six months.
facts.quote: your goal might be to increase online sales by 20% over six months, or get 30 new customer leads per month.

facts.fact: The article's example business goal is to get 30 new customer leads per month.
facts.quote: or get 30 new customer leads per month.

facts.fact: The article gives an example of a home improvement business's target audience as local homeowners between 35 and 65 years old.
facts.quote: you’re likely looking for local homeowners between 35 and 65 years old.

facts.fact: The article states a marketing budget may be a flat dollar amount per month or a percentage of projected revenue.
facts.quote: This might be a flat dollar amount per month or a percentage of your projected revenue.

facts.fact: Local Services Ads uses a pay-per-lead model, under which the advertiser pays only when a customer contacts them directly by phone, text, or email.
facts.quote: Pay-per-lead (PPL): You pay only when a customer contacts you directly via phone, text, or email.

facts.fact: Google Ads reaches audiences across Google's network including Search, Display, YouTube, and Gmail, according to the article.
facts.quote: enabling you to reach audiences across Google’s extensive network, including Search, Display, YouTube, and Gmail.

facts.fact: Local Services Ads does not require the advertiser to have a website.
facts.quote: No. Local Services Ads lets you manage leads directly without a website.

facts.fact: Local Services Ads features a Google Guarantee, Google Screened, or License Verified by Google badge, which Google Ads does not inherently carry.
facts.quote: Features a prominent Google Guarantee, Google Screened, or License Verified by Google badge, establishing credibility.

facts.fact: Local Services Ads appear at the very top of Google Search results and Google Maps for service-related queries.
facts.quote: Ads appear at the very top of Google Search results and Google Maps for service-related queries.

facts.fact: Google Ads offers text, image, and video ad formats.
facts.quote: choose from various formats like text, image, and video.

facts.fact: Google Ads uses a pay-per-click model, so the advertiser controls spend based on clicks.
facts.quote: Google Ads gives you a flexible pay-per-click model so you can control your spend based on clicks.

facts.fact: Local Services Ads uses a pay-per-lead model in which the advertiser pays only when customers contact the business.
facts.quote: Local Services Ads uses a pay-per-lead model where you only pay when customers contact you

facts.fact: Google Guarantee, Google Screened, and License Verified by Google badges indicate that a business, including its relevant licenses and insurance, has been verified by Google.
facts.quote: These badges indicate that your business, including relevant licenses and insurance, has been verified by Google.

facts.fact: Using Google Ads custom match audiences built from Local Services Ads leads requires first-party consent under Google's Customer Match policy.
facts.quote: Provided you obtained the necessary first-party consent required by Google’s Customer Match policy

facts.fact: Local Services Ads is intended for businesses that provide eligible services directly to local customers in a specific area.
facts.quote: directly to local customers in a specific area

facts.fact: Local Services Ads is designed to be less hands-on, requiring minimal management after setup, while Google Ads requires more active management.
facts.quote: It’s designed to be less hands-on and help you get seen in your area with minimal management once you’re set up.
